captions.instagram:
How does a water heater (geyser) work?

A geyser is a flask with a 2 kW heater inside, and it quietly uses physics you can feel in the shower: hot water floats, water expands, and a magnesium rod dies to save the tank. Take one apart in 3D.

→ A storage geyser is a steel tank in foam, with a 2 kW heating rod inside.
→ Instant geysers hold just 3 litres; gas geysers heat water as it flows.
→ Warming 15 L from 20 to 45 °C takes 1.57 million joules: about 14 minutes at 2 kW.
→ Winter water starts colder, so the same geyser takes about twice as long.
→ Hot water is 1.5% lighter than cold, so it floats in a layer on top.

youtubeLong.title: How does a water heater (geyser) work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A geyser is a flask with a 2 kW heater inside, and it quietly uses physics you can feel in the shower: hot water floats, water expands, and a magnesium rod dies to save the tank. Take one apart in 3D.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/waterheaterclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/waterheaterclear

In this video:
• A flask with a heater inside. A storage geyser is a steel tank lined with glass, wrapped in foam and hung on the wall.
• Water is hard to heat. Every litre needs 4,180 joules for each degree.
• Hot water floats. Water at 60 °C is about 1.5% lighter than at 20 °C, so the tank sorts itself into layers.
• Four things stand guard. The thermostat does the everyday work.
• A rod that dies for the tank. A magnesium anode corrodes instead of the steel, so it has to be replaced every year or two.
• Cheaper hot water. A hot tank leaks heat all day, which is what India's BEE star label measures.
